candidate.answerReason: The meetings total 135 minutes out of a 540-minute work day, giving 25%.

methods.label: Compare meeting time with the whole day
methods.explanation:
Use minutes for both the meeting time and the work day. The second meeting lasted \(2\cdot45=90\) minutes, so the meetings together lasted \(45+90=135\) minutes. Her work day lasted \(9\cdot60=540\) minutes. Therefore the percentage spent in meetings was
\[
\frac{135}{540}\cdot100\%
=\frac14\cdot100\%
=\boxed{25\%},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary time conversion and a part-to-whole percentage.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is calculating what percentage a part represents of a whole. Converting hours to minutes makes the quantities comparable, while percentage meaning and fraction-to-percentage conversion support interpreting the quotient.
